claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy containing tungsten, niobium, molybdenum, and tantalum can serve as a low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Careful control of the alloy's isotopic composition can reduce its long-term radioactivity.
The proposed alloy has microstructural stability at elevated temperatures.
The selected elements can be homogeneously distributed in a refractory HEA produced in powder or cast form.
Tailoring the elemental composition of a tungsten-based refractory HEA can minimize the production of long-lived radioactive isotopes.
The proposed material is intended to operate above 1000°C under high fusion-relevant neutron flux and plasma-edge transients.
Nano- to microscale phase stability and favorable grain-boundary character resist radiation-induced segregation.
Nano- to microscale phase stability and favorable grain-boundary character resist void swelling.
The proposed microstructure maintains mechanical integrity at high temperatures.
The multi-principal-element design produces sluggish diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion stabilizes the alloy microstructure under high temperature and irradiation.
Selecting low-activation isotopes reduces the generation or longevity of radioactive species.
The proposed alloy will have better high-temperature mechanical performance than conventional tungsten or high-activation alloys.
The proposed alloy will have greater irradiation resistance than conventional tungsten or high-activation alloys.
The proposed alloy will have lower post-service activation than conventional tungsten or high-activation alloys.
Improved mechanical performance, irradiation resistance, and reduced activation will prolong component lifespan and simplify waste management.
Pure tungsten and standard refractory alloys typically have higher activation or less tailored microstructural stability than the proposed alloy.
The predicted benefits depend on neutron damage remaining below the alloy's intrinsic resistance to radiation-induced phase changes.
Extreme irradiation or unanticipated phase transformations could negate the proposed benefits.
